svg.title: What DeeCure does: look deep, see it, fix it, optimize
svg.desc: A short story of what DeeCure does, in the app's own look. Is your Linux computer really healthy? DeeCure checks 10 layers, with more than 150 readings, 56 warnings, and 48 fixes with undo. Step 1, look deep: a scan beam walks down the layers: apps and processes; services, start-up, and jobs; containers; packages and updates; network; security, accounts, and privacy; storage and backups; kernel, drivers, and firmware; power, battery, and sleep; and hardware and devices, and finds 2 things to look at. Step 2, see it at a glance: a health score of 92, live CPU, memory, temperature, and network readings, and what needs you: the firewall is off, the main disk is full in about 12 days, and the SSD has 92% of its life left. Step 3, fix it safely: the problem is explained in plain English, the exact command (sudo ufw enable) is shown first, the fix is applied and checked again, the score goes from 92 to 97, and it can be undone. Step 4, optimize: 12 improvements this computer needs, each with a preview. DeeCure is free and open source, for Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 LTS.

g.text: The answer is spread across many
